title: Data Privacy & Security Fundamentals
description: A three-chapter interactive course teaching employees the essentials of data privacy regulations, threat awareness, and secure day-to-day workflows.

style_guide.illustration_style: flat vector, isometric accents, brand-blue palette

chapters.title: Understanding Data Privacy
chapters.objective: Explain the core principles of data privacy (GDPR, CCPA) and identify the types of personal data your organisation handles.

blocks.text: Illustration of a shield protecting personal data icons (name, email, location)

Every day Acme Corp processes thousands of records containing personal information. A single breach can cost millions in fines, erode customer trust, and trigger regulatory investigations. This chapter explains the legal landscape and your role in keeping data safe.

turns.speaker: Compliance Officer
turns.text: Did you know that under GDPR a fine can reach 4% of global annual revenue?

turns.speaker: New Hire
turns.text: That sounds enormous. How do we avoid that?

turns.speaker: Compliance Officer
turns.text: By understanding what personal data is, where it lives, and who can access it. That is exactly what this course covers.

blocks.text: How Data Flows Through the Organisation

steps.label: Collection
steps.description: Data enters via web forms, APIs, or manual entry. Consent must be recorded at this stage.

steps.label: Processing
steps.description: Systems transform, enrich, or aggregate data. Access is restricted by role-based controls.

steps.label: Storage
steps.description: Encrypted at rest in approved data centres. Retention limits are enforced automatically.

steps.label: Sharing
steps.description: Shared only under a Data Processing Agreement (DPA). Cross-border transfers require Standard Contractual Clauses.

steps.label: Deletion
steps.description: Automated purge after the retention window. A certificate of destruction is logged for audit.

blocks.text: Remember: data you cannot classify, you cannot protect. Always tag new datasets with a classification level before processing.

data.title: Maximum Fine as % of Revenue by Regulation

panels.body: Applies to any organisation processing EU residents' data. Key rights: access, erasure, portability. Requires a Data Protection Officer (DPO) in many cases.
Grants California consumers the right to know, delete, and opt-out of sale of their personal information. Enforced by the California AG.
Closely modelled on GDPR. Introduces 10 legal bases for processing and mandates a DPO equivalent (Encarregado).

questions.question: What is the maximum GDPR fine as a percentage of global annual revenue?
questions.explanation: Under GDPR Art. 83(5), fines can reach up to 4% of worldwide annual turnover.

questions.question: At which stage of the data lifecycle must consent be recorded?
questions.explanation: Consent must be obtained and recorded at the point of data collection.

questions.question: What does DPA stand for in a data-sharing context?
questions.explanation: A Data Processing Agreement governs the terms under which personal data is shared with a third-party processor.

questions.question: Which regulation grants consumers an explicit right to opt-out of the sale of personal information?
questions.explanation: The CCPA specifically provides a 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' right.

chapters.title: Threat Awareness & Prevention
chapters.objective: Recognise common attack vectors (phishing, social engineering, malware) and apply preventive measures in daily work.

pages.title: The Anatomy of a Phishing Attack

blocks.text: Annotated screenshot of a phishing email highlighting red flags (spoofed sender, urgency language, suspicious link)

data.image_alt: A realistic phishing email annotated with interactive hotspots

regions.label: Spoofed sender
regions.detail: The display name says 'IT Support' but the actual address is it-supp0rt@malicio.us. Always check the full address.

regions.label: Urgency language
regions.detail: 'Your account will be locked in 2 hours' is a pressure tactic. Legitimate IT notices give at least 7 days.

regions.label: Suspicious link
regions.detail: Hover to see the real URL: http://acme-hr.fakesite.ru/login. The domain does not match acme-corp.com.

regions.label: Generic greeting
regions.detail: 'Dear Employee' instead of your real name is a strong indicator of a mass-phishing campaign.

blocks.text: Attackers do not always use email. They may call, visit in person, or use messaging apps. The goal is always the same: trick you into revealing credentials or granting access.

cards.back: The attacker fabricates a scenario (e.g. 'I'm from the auditing firm') to gain trust and extract information.
Following an authorised person through a secure door without badging in. Always challenge unknown visitors.
Leaving an infected USB stick in a common area hoping someone plugs it in. Never use unknown removable media.
Offering something (free software, tech support) in exchange for login credentials or remote access.

data.prompt: You receive an email from 'ceo@acme-c0rp.com' asking you to urgently wire $15,000 to a new vendor. What do you do?

branches.choice: Wire the money immediately — the CEO must need it urgently.
branches.feedback: Never act on financial requests received by email alone. This is a classic CEO-fraud / Business Email Compromise (BEC) attack. The spoofed domain 'acme-c0rp.com' (with a zero) is a red flag.

branches.choice: Reply to the email asking for confirmation.
branches.feedback: Good instinct to verify, but replying goes back to the attacker. Instead, contact the CEO through a known, independent channel (phone, Slack, in person).

branches.choice: Verify via a separate channel (call the CEO directly) and report the email to security@acme-corp.com.
branches.feedback: Excellent! Out-of-band verification defeats BEC attacks. Reporting the email lets the security team block the sender and warn others.

branches.choice: Delete the email and ignore it.
branches.feedback: Deleting protects you, but other colleagues may also receive the same email. Always report suspicious emails so the security team can act.

blocks.text: Attack Trends Over the Last Four Years

data.title: Reported Security Incidents at Acme Corp (2022-2025)

blocks.text: Phishing incidents dropped 65% after mandatory awareness training was introduced in 2023. Your participation in this course contributes directly to this trend.

questions.question: What is the FIRST thing you should do when you receive a suspicious financial request by email?
options: Wire the money to avoid delays
Reply to the sender to confirm
Verify via an independent channel and report to security
Forward it to a colleague for a second opinion
questions.explanation: Always verify financial requests through a separate, trusted channel (phone, in person) and report the email to the security team.

questions.question: Which social engineering tactic involves following someone through a secure door?
questions.explanation: Tailgating (or piggybacking) is the act of following an authorised person through a controlled access point.

questions.question: What red flag indicates a spoofed email domain?
options: Email is sent during business hours
The domain contains character substitutions (e.g. '0' for 'o')
The email has a company logo
The email is written in English
questions.explanation: Attackers register look-alike domains with subtle character substitutions. Always inspect the full sender address.

chapters.title: Secure Workflows in Practice
chapters.objective: Apply secure-by-default habits to password management, file sharing, remote access, and incident reporting.

blocks.text: Infographic comparing weak vs strong passwords with entropy scores

data.prompt: Drag each practice to the correct category: SECURE or INSECURE.

items.text: Use a unique 16+ character passphrase per service
Reuse your email password for the company VPN
Enable hardware-key MFA on all critical accounts
Write passwords on a sticky note under your keyboard
Store credentials in an approved password manager
Share your login via unencrypted email

steps.label: 1. Classify
steps.description: Determine the sensitivity of the document (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted).

steps.label: 2. Choose channel
steps.description: Use the approved platform for the classification level (e.g. SharePoint for Confidential, encrypted transfer for Restricted).

steps.label: 3. Set permissions
steps.description: Grant least-privilege access. Use time-limited links where possible.

steps.label: 4. Audit
steps.description: Verify the access log within 24 hours. Revoke access once the recipient confirms receipt.

blocks.text: 60-second screencast showing how to connect to the corporate VPN and verify the encrypted tunnel.
What To Do When Something Goes Wrong
Every employee is the first line of defence. Reporting an incident quickly reduces its blast radius and helps the security team contain it.

data.image_alt: Screenshot of the Acme Corp incident-reporting portal with annotated regions

regions.label: Severity selector
regions.detail: Choose P1 (data breach confirmed) through P4 (informational). The SLA clock starts when you submit.

regions.label: Affected systems
regions.detail: Tag every system involved. This auto-notifies the owning team and triggers the relevant runbook.

regions.label: Evidence upload
regions.detail: Attach screenshots, email headers, or log snippets. Do NOT paste credentials or PII into this field.

panels.body: Notify security@acme-corp.com AND your manager immediately. Do not power off affected systems — forensic evidence may be lost.
Submit the incident form within 1 hour. Isolate the affected device from the network if safe to do so.
Submit within 24 hours. Include the policy reference and any corrective action already taken.
Log for awareness. No SLA, but review by the security team within 5 business days.

questions.question: Which of the following is a SECURE password practice?
options: Using a unique 16+ character passphrase per service
questions.explanation: Long, unique passphrases stored in an approved password manager provide the strongest protection.

questions.question: What is the FIRST step before sharing a file externally?
options: Email the file as an attachment
Post it on the public wiki
questions.explanation: Classification determines which channel and access controls are appropriate for the document.

questions.question: When should a P1 incident be reported?
questions.explanation: A confirmed breach (P1) requires immediate notification to security and management.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when a system is suspected of being compromised?
questions.explanation: Powering off can destroy volatile forensic evidence (RAM, running processes). Isolate the network connection instead.
